description:
Problem (owner 2026-10-27: 'you MUST ensure that we have meaningful testing of the oracle review process that is not vacuous'): three defects reached production or review because tests stubbed the boundary they claimed to prove: the concedes skeleton (tests built Python booleans, never filled the rendered template), the six-day pool block (quota reset attributed to the configured pool and carried across heads; no test ran two runs and a new head), the pr-arm/pr-rerun loop (no test ran arm while full CI was in progress). test_local_review stubs reachable(); sweep tests mock verdict_runs; two tests asserted only truthiness of response_template. The 40 oracle test files are unit-level; no test drives the workflow's real sequence. mutmut is configured (pyproject [tool.mutmut], make mutation-test) but covers no oracle module.

Outcome:
(1) Scenario harness under tests/integration/oracle/ (or the repo's integration convention): runs the real cli commands as subprocesses in the workflow's order (plan, select, attempts, finalize, post, guard, gate evaluate, sweep, local-review) against (a) a stateful fake GitHub HTTP server reached through the real github.py code (reviews with node ids and edit flags, statuses with creators, review threads, workflow runs with pagination and total_count, artifacts, 5xx injection), (b) a fake omp executable that emits the pinned OMP build's JSON event-stream shape taken from recorded real runs and answers by filling the actually rendered response template the way a model does (replace angle-bracket placeholders with strings, keep nulls and literals), with scripted failures (429 from a fallback provider with reset text, malformed JSON, incomplete, empty, timeout), (c) real templates, policy, OMP config and real git repositories for diffs. Assertions are operator-visible: posted status state and text, review body, retry state, gate conclusion, dispatched runs.
(2) Scenarios: first review SHIP and gate success; follow-up with prior defects (model-style fill validates); dispute round; quota 429 from a fallback provider then a new head (pool not blocked beyond the cap); edited App review -> HOLD; byte-identical carry and carry whose App status disagrees -> HOLD; invalid reply recovery; sweep with failed runs, stale same-head state, listing 5xx and a >1000-run listing; pr-arm while the full CI run is in progress; two concurrent local reviews of different patches. A scenario whose fix is not merged yet is added by that fix's PR, not marked xfail.
(3) Bug replay: each scenario names the defect it guards and is proven to fail when that defect is reintroduced (apply the known bad change to an export and run the scenario).
(4) Mutation gate: add the oracle modules (selection, protocol, absence, retry, sweep, verdict, render, evidence, attempts, report, oracle_review_check, soundness_merge_digest) to mutmut; record the baseline kill rate; surviving mutants in decision logic (anything that changes a decision, status, dispatch or block) are each killed by a new test or recorded as equivalent with a reason; a make target runs it for oracle code.
(5) Vacuity audit of the existing oracle tests: list tests that mock the behaviour they assert, assert only truthiness or non-emptiness, or echo mocks; rewrite or delete each (repo policy: delete, never re-pin, wording or incidental tests).
(6) Captured real outputs (owner 2026-10-27: 'Using real OMP quota in a test is unacceptable. Only Jev usage is acceptable in tests. Capture real outputs and use them for the test harnesses'): add a capture path that keeps the redacted raw OMP event stream, stderr excerpt and terminal error event of every real reviewer attempt that already runs (CI oracle-verdict attempts and local pr-open reviews) as an artifact; curate captured streams (successful replies, follow-up replies with prior defects, dispute replies, invalid replies, quota/auth/timeout errors from primary and fallback providers) into versioned, redacted harness fixtures. Tests never call OMP or a model provider; Jev calls are allowed in tests only where the feature under test is Jev classification.

Decision gates:
1. Owner decision 2026-10-27: no live model canary and no OMP quota in any test; only Jev may be called. If a scenario cannot be driven without a captured real output that does not exist yet, record the gap and capture it from the next real run instead of inventing the shape.
2. If the mutation baseline for decision logic is below 70%, report the surviving-mutant list to the owner before choosing a target threshold.
3. If running the harness in CI would exceed the medium tier's time budget, ask where it should run.

Item guardrails: no network to GitHub or model providers from the harness (fake server and fake omp only); fixtures come only from captured real runs, never hand-invented shapes, and are redacted (redaction_check passes on every fixture); no OMP or provider call in tests; Jev only for Jev features; harness tests are deterministic and full-suite safe; every scenario asserts operator-visible outcomes, never internal call counts.
